title: Savolaisia sutkauksia ja letkauksia
summary: "Savolaisia sutkauksia ja letkauksia" by Juudas Puustinen and Ernst Lampén is a collection of regional humor, dialect sketches, and essays written in the early 20th century. The volume celebrates Savonian wit and identity through sayings, anecdotes, poems, and short prose, mixing playful wordcraft with affectionate observations on local life, language, and customs. The opening of the collection frames its mission with a jocular “letter” from Imppa Ryynänen, blessing the gathering of Savonian quips and urging readers to keep both levity and warmth of heart. A satirical tableau of Christmas peace follows, softening political feuds, clerical thunder, schoolroom strictness, and household squabbles for one holiday moment. An essay then asks whether elementary schools are eroding the Savo dialect, contrasting priests’ old murre-sermons with standardizing classrooms while defending Savonian “holy lightness” as a lifeline in hardship. Short verses and quickfire jokes punctuate the flow, and the sharp-tongued boatman Ukko-Riekko steps onstage before a lively night scene on Lake Saimaa, where nautical banter and near-collision comedy unfold in rich dialect. A farcical fishing tale powered by “96%” spirits, absurdist one-liners, and a roguish deathbed pun lead into brisk Kuopio vignettes skewering harbor chaos, street “cleanliness,” and runaway rumors. The excerpt rounds out with tiny dialogues and dialect poems that praise regional foods (kalakukko, talakkuna), landscapes, and courtship, before tapering off amid more lake-travel quips.
